copy.title: The Ice Cream Tragedy
copy.objective: Learning that you can't fix a melted cone, but you can fix a melted mood using Mirror Neurons.

copy.text: The tragedy struck at exactly 14:03 on Tuesday on the Sidewalk of Doom. The sun was melting the asphalt. Mimi was digging frantically in her gigantic bag that contained half the house. She let out a long, exhausted breath, trying to keep her own inner grumpy monster from waking up in the heat. She was shining a bright flashlight into the dark depths of the bag.
Where is my phone?! Is it under the spare shoes or the emergency lasagna? I can't find it anywhere! I need to call Grandma!
Mammi, you are using your phone's flashlight to look for your phone.
Oh. Right. It's a tactical search light. I knew that.

Mimi did a quick 'Wet Dog Shake' with her hands to physically throw off the stress. Meanwhile, Alio was holding the Holy Grail of summer: a triple-scoop Choco-Mint-Explosion cone. And then... gravity attacked. SPLAT. The ice cream hit the sidewalk face down. It wasn't just a fall; it was a crime scene.
NOOOO! My life is over! It's bleeding chocolate! The ants are eating my happiness! And Dilo said if an ant eats sugar, it mutates into a giant monster and stomps on toes!
It's true. I saw a documentary on YouTube. And yesterday I tried to charge my phone by rubbing it on the cat to create static electricity, so I know science. You better run, Alio.
Alio turned pale, his eyes wide with terror. He scrambled behind Nini's legs.
Save me! I don't want to be squished by a mutant ant!
Nini, wearing a tulle skirt and cat ears, stomped her glittery sneaker.

copy.text: Dilo! Stop it! Ants don't mutate, and Alio's heart is shattered into a million pieces!

Alio, don't listen to him. The only thing that happened is that the cat got so static-charged she is now a magnet. She walked through the living room and every piece of dust, glitter, and popcorn stuck to her fur. She looks like a walking vacuum cleaner bag.
But Dilo looked so professional!
Nini crouched down next to Alio, looking like a tiny, sad meringue.

copy.text: Alio, look at me. Forget the ants. Your invisible energy bucket just tipped over, didn't it?
I don't have a bucket. I don't have anything. Just a puddle.
Nini sat down right next to him on the hot pavement and pointed above his head.

It sits right here. Everybody has one. It's invisible. When it's full, you feel brave and kind. When it's empty, everything feels extra loud and unfair. I can't fill mine just by wishing. But when I pour kindness into your bucket, my brain releases happy chemicals that fill mine too! It's like wireless charging or like magic WI-FI!
Emergency refill protocol! Nini wrapped Alio in a tactical 'Mega-Squeeze' hug.
I'm not fixing the ice cream. I'm just sitting in the sadness with you until your bucket refills. Now, try to make a smile. Even a fake one. Just lift the corners of your mouth.
Alio made a wobbly, weird grimace. It looked funny. He giggled a tiny bit through his tears.
See? Your face muscles just sent a text message to your brain saying 'We are smiling, so things must be okay!'
Alio took a deep, shuddering breath. The problem wasn't gone, but he wasn't alone anymore. And that made all the difference. Alio Status Update: Battery +10%. Sadness Reduced.
Touching moment, guys. Now, if you'll excuse me, I'm going to find the cat. If I rub her fast enough against the carpet, I think I can power the entire neighborhood.

copy.heading: THE BRAIN SECRET (The Copycat Cells)
copy.science: Your brain has special tiny radar sensors called 'Mirror Neurons.' They help you 'catch' other people's feelings. When you see a friend cry, your brain practices that feeling so you can understand them.
copy.in_story: Remember when Nini crouched down and looked sad with Alio? That was her Mirror Neurons working! She didn't just watch him; she felt a little bit of his sadness so she could help him.

copy.heading: THE TOOL ('The Silent Sit')
copy.science: Sometimes words don't work. By just sitting calmly near a sad person, your slow breathing acts like a remote control that helps slow down their racing heart.
copy.in_story: Nini said, 'I'm not fixing the ice cream. I'm just sitting in the sadness with you.' She didn't buy him a new cone immediately; she just sat on the hot pavement. Her calm body helped Alio's body stop panicking.

copy.heading: THE GLITCH ('The Face Trick')
copy.science: This is the 'Fake It 'Til You Make It' trick. If you force your face muscles to smile, they send a signal to your brain saying, 'Hey! We are smiling! Release the happy chemicals!'
copy.in_story: Nini told Alio to make a 'fake smile.' Even though Alio was sad, making the wobbly grimace actually made him giggle. His face tricked his brain into feeling 1% better!

copy.heading: TALK ABOUT IT
copy.in_story: Alio admitted his bucket was empty ('Just a puddle').
copy.your_turn: Is your bucket full, half-full, or empty right now? Who did you see today who looked like they had 'low battery'?

copy.heading: FAMILY MISSION
copy.in_story: Nini recharged Alio with a 'Mega-Squeeze' hug.
copy.your_turn: Find someone today who needs a refill. Do one tiny thing (smile, wave, share, hug) to recharge them.

copy.heading: TOP SECRET SCIENCE (For Big and Small Brains)
copy.body: Did you know feelings are contagious? When Nini sat calmly next to Alio, her slow heartbeat sent a secret invisible signal to Alio's body that said 'It is safe now.' This helped him calm down without using any words. Scientists call this Co-regulation, but we just call it 'sharing your calm'.

copy.meaning: My emotional bucket is EMPTY. I am sad, or overwhelmed. I'm glitching and don't have the strength to fix anything right now.
copy.operation: The Family Team activates immediately the: Refill & Hug operation (aka Magic WI-FI).
copy.parent_says: 'Stop crying, it's just ice cream, we will buy another one!',
copy.teach_to_say: 'Your bucket spilled. I am just going to sit here in the sadness with you until it refills.'
